literal: Those who transgress dead people are like; anger those who renounced ascetics equal.
translation: Those who transgress through anger are like the dead. Those who have renounced anger are equal to ascetics who have renounced everything.
modern: சினத்தால் நன்னடத்தை வரம்பை மீறியவர்கள் இறந்தவர்களுக்கு ஒப்பானவர்கள். சினத்தை விட்டொழித்தவர்கள் முற்றும் துறந்த முனிவர்களுக்கு ஒப்பானவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts those who yield to anger with those who conquer it. The word 'இறந்தார்' is used twice: first to mean those who transgress the limits of good conduct through anger, and second to mean the dead, implying that angry people are as good as dead. Similarly, 'துறந்தார்' is used twice: first for those who have renounced anger, and second for ascetics who have renounced the world, showing that conquering anger is as great as ultimate renunciation.
